clue.text: Unlucky individual suddenly turns on the radio

indicators.note: what is broadcast on the radio is only heard, so the word is identified by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to jink is to dodge with a quick sudden turn, as a winger or a hunted hare does

explanation.surface: A hapless person abruptly switches on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: JINKS, quick evasive swerves, sounds exactly like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinx is a person or thing believed to bring bad luck to those around them, so an unlucky presence.

clue.text: Spooner's tummy sits above his trousers; that'll be the candies

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words are exchanged

blocks.note: belly is a tummy; it takes the other word's opening sound
surface padding placing one word before the other
jeans are trousers; it takes the first word's opening sound

explanation.surface: A man's paunch hangs over his waistband, which the sweets will have caused.
explanation.walkthrough: BELLY JEANS with initial sounds swapped becomes the sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly beans are small bean-shaped sugary sweets, a kind of candy.

clue.text: Latino at home about to preserve a meat sauce?

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for at home is read backwards
to preserve here is to put in a can, so the sauce goes inside the container word

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
with preserve, to can means to seal food in a tin to keep it
a ragu is an Italian meat sauce for pasta

explanation.surface: A Hispanic cook at home is about to bottle some bolognese.
explanation.walkthrough: To can food is to preserve it by sealing it inside a tin, which is why 'preserve' can signal putting one thing inside another. The question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nicaraguan comes from a Central American country and is a Latino, a person of Latin American origin.

clue.text: Composed requiems featuring a very brief piece of music

indicators.note: music that is composed is put together and arranged, so the letters here are arranged afresh
featuring means including, so the following short words join the letters to be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
v is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone wrote requiems that include a tiny musical fragment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on from the wordplay: 'a very' supplies two letters to the anagram and also opens the definition's phrasing.
explanation.definitionFit: A semiquaver is a sixteenth note, one of the shortest note values in ordinary notation, so a very brief musical unit.

clue.text: In Basel, I'm in a team to deliver a knockout blow

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the city name to the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A Swiss footballer in Basel is on the side that knocks out its rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate a team is to knock them out of a competition, so to deliver a knockout blow.

clue.text: Music genre fashionable festival served up

indicators.note: in a down clue anything sent up is read from bottom to top, so the festival is written backwards

blocks.note: in means fashionable
Eid is a Muslim festival

explanation.surface: A trendy kind of music was on the bill at a festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Indie is a style of rock and pop music, originally from independent record labels.

clue.text: FT tag line run in a way that's quite critical

indicators.note: done in a way suggests a different arrangement, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper's slogan was published in a fairly scathing manner.
explanation.walkthrough: FT is the Financial Times, the paper that runs this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Unflattering remarks fail to praise and so are somewhat negative, close to quite critical.

clue.text: Extremely light pistol manufacturer

blocks.note: first meaning: to a high degree
second meaning: Edward ..., the American naval officer who devised the flare gun firing coloured signal lights

explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a signal flare fired from a Very pistol, named after its inventor; 'light' looks like a weight but belongs to the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb for an extreme degree shares its spelling with the inventor's surname, given to the flare and its pistol.

clue.text: Odd characters in Royal Hospital blocking Welsh settlement

indicators.note: odd characters are those in first, third, fifth position, so every other letter is taken
blocking means getting in the way, so the hospital letter is wedged inside

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Eccentric people at a Royal Hospital obstruct a Welsh village.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhyl is a seaside resort on the north coast of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyl is a town in Denbighshire, a settlement in the sense of an inhabited place.

clue.text: Beat music played on a guitar?

blocks.note: first meaning: to defeat or thrash
second meaning: a short melodic phrase or riff played by a guitarist

explanation.surface: Rhythmic music performed on a guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Beat' a musical rhythm, but it is the verb to defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To lick is informal for defeating someone, and a lick is a jazz and rock term for a short instrumental phrase.

clue.text: Derby rip-off almost ruined 15, for one

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word before is dropped
something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so the letters are put back in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A swindle at the Derby horse race goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 15-across, EAGLE. The Derby is a famous English horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a classic example of a raptor, the hunting birds with hooked beaks and talons.

clue.text: Maybe illness affected an area of industrial production?

indicators.note: something affected has been altered, so the letters before are changed in order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps sickness hit a part of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' looks like illness striking a workplace, but it rearranges the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly line is a factory sequence of workstations where a product is built, a zone of manufacturing.

clue.text: Northerner bowls muscular chap after collecting one run

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the muscular chap takes the following letters inside him

blocks.note: in cricket to york a batter is to bowl them out with a yorker, a ball pitched at their feet
a he-man is a strongly built, macho man
Roman numeral one
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A northern cricketer bowls at a strongman once he has scored a single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowls' looks like the lawn game but is cricket: a yorker is a ball pitched at the batter's toes. Yorkshire is a large county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkshireman comes from Yorkshire in the north of England, so is a typical northerner.

clue.text: Second go: draw constant energy, love

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
to go, informally, is to urinate, to wee
a tie is a drawn game
pi is the mathematical constant
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rematch has ended level, a steady supply of power, my dear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' and 'draw' look like turns in a game; one is the nursery word for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetie pie is an affectionate form of address, used like love or darling.

clue.text: Plant owner slept around

indicators.note: around suggests moving about in no fixed order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A proprietor was promiscuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slept around' reads as one phrase about promiscuity; only 'around' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleenwort is a fern of the genus Asplenium, once thought to cure spleen ailments, so a plant.

clue.text: Each golf hole halved? Great score!

indicators.note: halved means cut down to half, so only one half of each word before it is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
Golf is the NATO alphabet word for G
taken as written

explanation.surface: Splitting each hole in a golf match gives a fine result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Halved' covers both each and hole: the first half of one and the second half of the other survive. In golf a halved hole is a tie, which is the surface's disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an eagle is a hole completed two strokes under par, an excellent result.

clue.text: In recession, hands Tessa a financial derivative

indicators.note: something in recession is going back, so the words that follow are read backwards

blocks.note: paws is a jokey word for hands
taken as written

explanation.surface: During an economic downturn, someone gives Tessa an investment product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In recession' sounds economic, fitting the FT, but it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset swap is a derivative contract exchanging the cash flows of an asset, typically a fixed-rate bond, for floating-rate payments.

clue.text: Divert branch line?

blocks.note: first meaning: to distract from the main subject
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning splits the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack is to deflect from a purpose, and a side track is literally a subsidiary railway route.

clue.text: Older lady saving American money as a bit on the side?

indicators.note: saving means keeping something safe within, so the older lady holds the next letter inside

blocks.note: nan is a familiar British word for a grandmother
A is a standard abbreviation for American
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: A grandmother hoarding dollars as a secret lover sounds like a racy story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit on the side' usually means a secret lover; here it is a side dish served with a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is an Indian flatbread usually served alongside a curry, so it is literally a side order.

clue.text: Bailiff let off pair I evicted

indicators.note: evicted means thrown out, so the pair and the I are removed from the longer word

blocks.note: to reprieve someone is to let them off a punishment
pr is the abbreviation for pair
taken as written

explanation.surface: An official lets off a couple after kicking the speaker out of their home.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing P, R and I from REPRIEVE leaves REEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval English official, a steward or bailiff who managed a manor or district.

clue.text: Poor BP results reported following a period of inflation

definitions.text: Poor BP results reported following a period of inflation

blocks.clueFragment: Poor BP results reported following a period of inflation
blocks.note: surface reading: an oil company's bad profit figures announced after an economic spell of rising prices

blocks.clueFragment: Poor BP results reported following a period of inflation
blocks.note: setter's reading: a bad blood pressure reading given after the doctor's cuff has been pumped up on your arm

explanation.surface: The oil giant BP announces poor results after a spell of rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: BP looks like the oil company and inflation like economics, an apt trap in the FT; really BP is blood pressure and the inflation is of the measuring cuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypertension is the medical term for persistently high blood pressure, a poor reading when measured.

clue.text: South American woman due to arrive about 6

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the number is placed inside the arrival abbreviation

blocks.note: ETA is estimated time of arrival
Roman numeral six

explanation.surface: A woman from South America is expected around six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6-down but is just the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita was the nickname of Eva Perón, the Argentine first lady, a famous South American woman.

clue.text: Small dog shaking tail that's dirty

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun: something that is dirty

indicators.note: shaking off its tail means the dog loses its final letter

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for small
a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A little dog wagging its filthy tail.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog shaking its tail sounds like wagging, but here the tail is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is soot or grime and also obscene material, both things considered dirty.

clue.text: City of Athens marketplace that's out of the ordinary?

indicators.note: out of here means removed from, so the ordinary letter is taken away

blocks.note: the agora was the public square and market of ancient Athens
o is an abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: A city whose Athenian market is something unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the ordinary' reads as an idiom for unusual, but it is split to strip a letter. Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in Uttar Pradesh, northern India, home of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Paean to Mary, a gift Cain distributed after Mass

indicators.note: things distributed are spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: m is the abbreviation for mass in physics
taken as written

explanation.surface: After church Mass, Cain hands out presents while a hymn to the Virgin plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' fits the church scene but is the physics abbreviation. Strictly the Magnificat is Mary's own song praising God, not a song to her, as the setter later admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magnificat is the canticle of Mary from Luke's Gospel, a hymn of praise sung at evening services.

clue.text: Counterpart at work unaffected by setback

indicators.note: a word not changed by being set back, read from the end, is the same both ways round

blocks.note: the definition itself supplies the word, which is checked by reading it backwards
the word must read identically in either direction

explanation.surface: A colleague in a matching job shrugs off a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the answer's own symmetry; there is also a hint of OP, a work, joined by its own reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British informal slang, originally military, for a colleague or opposite number holding the equivalent post.

clue.text: Corporate names rush to withdraw electronic currency

indicators.note: to withdraw is to pull back, so the word for rush is taken backwards

blocks.note: to dart is to rush
e- is the prefix for electronic
the mark was the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Firms hurry to take digital money out of the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdraw' suggests a cash machine, but it turns the rush word around.
explanation.definitionFit: Trademarks are registered names or symbols that identify a company's goods, so they serve as corporate names.

clue.text: Relish stocked by Devizes Tesco

indicators.note: something stocked by a shop is held inside it, so the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A sauce sold in a Tesco supermarket in Devizes, a Wiltshire market town.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest means keen enjoyment or gusto, the same as relish in the sense of appetite for something.
